correctness.rationale: The exact finite attachment law is coupled to iid two-sided geometric lags, with summable modification probability and a uniform O(log n) future-edge discrepancy. Stationary leaf expectations and joint probabilities are exact independent-product identities; the covariance series is geometrically summable. The past/future sigma-fields are separated except for exponentially rare long edges, so Herrndorf strong-mixing FCLT applies. A disjoint Bernoulli decision conditioning gives the explicit nonzero asymptotic variance lower bound. Geometric-product Taylor summation proves the r-up-to-1 endpoint. The standalone verifier independently enumerates all finite parent sequences for n<=6 at three rational parameters and passed 838 assertions; enumeration is not the proof.

value.rationale: Leaf population is the natural global boundary statistic for the recent 2026 degree/leafdegree program, while exponential birth-label preference is a structurally distinct 2024-established recursive tree. The explicit negative-pair covariance and nondegenerate long-run variance quantify dependence not available from individual degree marginals. The singular weak-preference limit (e^-1 versus uniform 1/2 and e^-1-2e^-2 versus uniform 1/12) reveals noncommuting limits that affect using near-uniform attachment approximations. These are motivated structural asymptotics, not arbitrary parameter substitutions.
